correctness.rationale: For wheel W_{m+1}=K1∨C_m, m>=5, rim pairs distance 2 force both hub and intermediate rim vertex. Hence convex sets without hub are only empty, singletons, adjacent pairs, and hub-containing convex sets correspond exactly to rim 0/1 words avoiding local 101. A rim support cannot shatter if it contains a triple of cyclic consecutive rim vertices; otherwise every positive trace T is realized by including hub and making each designated negative rim vertex and at least one neighbor outside the support negative, so no 101 remains. Hub-containing supports have at most one queried rim vertex or two adjacent rim vertices by the hub-negative trace. The rim-support face numbers therefore equal D(C_m;z), with additional z+m z²+m z³. Marking a zero in cyclic words with ones-runs <=2 gives exact m/(m-k)[t^k](1+t+t²)^(m-k). Summing triple inequalities gives |S|<=floor(2m/3), achieved by runs of 110; hub triples tie at m=5 only. Independent actual geodesic convex-set enumeration verified the full support structure for m=5..9 and polynomial coefficients. This is a proof for every m>=5, not extrapolation from small wheels.

originality.rationale: The dissociation complex of a cycle is a classical combinatorial object, and the graph-convexity learning framework is also prior. The new scientific claim is the exact equivalence between all shattered geodesic-convex supports of a wheel and cyclic dissociation configurations together with precisely classified hub exceptions and exact face polynomial. The primary 2022 graph convex online-learning paper gives general bounds but not this wheel complex; 2023 dissociation enumeration is not itself a learning-theory shattering statement.
